display.title: Ne'ilah: Bring Us Home! The Princess and the Peasant
display.summary_short: Why do we cry out 'L'shanah haba'ah b'Yerushalayim' after the shofar at the end of Ne'ilah? The Dubno Maggid's parable of a princess married to a poor peasant explains.
display.summary_long: Between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, the storyteller looks at the prayer 'Shema Koleinu' and its plea 'Hashiveinu', bring us back to You, which he explains as asking Hashem to bring us home to the Beis HaMikdash, where we will serve Him properly. The same idea, he says, is behind the shout of 'L'shanah haba'ah b'Yerushalayim' after the final shofar blast of Ne'ilah. He tells the Dubno Maggid's parable: a choosy princess is married to a simple peasant, who makes her scrub floors and wash laundry in his town. When the king announces a visit, everything is polished, but she begs her father to take her home, because it will all go back to the way it was. Her husband explains he cannot give her what she deserves, and asks the king to bring them both to the palace. The Torah is Hashem's princess, given to the Jewish people. On Yom Kippur we are like angels, but the Torah fears what happens afterwards, so we ask Hashem to bring us to His palace, the Beis HaMikdash, with the Geulah.
display.lesson: We truly want to keep the Torah properly; we ask Hashem to bring the Geulah and take us home to the Beis HaMikdash, where we can.

date.note: Recorded after Rosh Hashanah and before Yom Kippur; closes with a wish that 5784 become the year of the Geulah.
